newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulls wait in wings as German bourse kicks off.
newsitem.headline: Bulls wait in wings as German bourse kicks off.

text.p: Germany's 30 share DAX index opened at record highs on Wednesday, boosted by a sturdy dollar whose strength outweighed any negative impact to sentiment from Wall Street's lower overnight close.

At 1011 GMT the DAX index, which tracks trade in the 30 blue-chip shares, was up 19.43 points, or 0.59 percent, at 3,340.09 points, just off a record high, as the DAX sought to catch up with its electronic IBIS counterpart.
There had been fears earlier of a correction after Tuesday's remarkable bull-run, but dealers breathed a sigh of relief after early electronic trade was stable.

"If a correction was going to happen it probably would have happened by now," said one Frankfurt trader, pointing to market resilience in the face of a possible hangover after Tuesday's sturdy bull run.
The main agent in staving off this hangover was the strength of the dollar against the mark at around 1.71.
The sturdy dollar mostly outweighed the negative effects of the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street closing nearly one percent lower overnight and a softer German debt market.
Shares in the limelight early on included Deutsche Lufthansa AG, which was up 5.65 percent at 24.30 marks in early bourse trade.
Traders had identified a large domestic buyer who was buying "massive" amounts of the stock. The stock was lifted by a Boeing report which forecast a 4.4 percent increase in air travel in Europe.
Diversified utility Veba AG was also higher early on, up 1.45 marks at 99.45 marks, as technical factors buoyed the stock.
